per_shot.note: Segmented faceted serpent with a white-hot head reads instantly at play size; its orange wash lands on the tunnel stone and sits in the VEIL amber family.

Chunky plated segments with ember underglow and a blazing mouth; the light pools on the surrounding blocks. The danger end is clear, but body segments read a little like flat cones rather than a living body.

Violet crystal crab with an open jaw is a readable threat and a deliberate cool accent against the amber, but it hovers off the rock and reads as a spider, not an ore that bites; its halo is lost against the lamp-lit wall.
Nice faceted crystal carapace and cyan crown; jaws read. Glow is a faint grey-white halo that barely tints the stone, and the near-black dark-violet legs fall into the background.

In the core chamber the pair of copper stick figures sinks into an already-orange scene; at play size they read as small mannequins with sparks, not a pursuer made of light. A dark smudge behind them looks like an artifact.

The faceted gaunt forms with white-hot hearts and ember motes are a strong idea, and the floor under them warms, but the bodies are darker than the chamber and the dark halo behind them reads as a bug.
Tight flock of ice-cyan shard birds with bright cores; their cyan light floods the floor in a clear pool. Very CRYOS, reads at play size, and glow lands.
Crisp faceted wings and bright cores; a saturated cyan wash on the ice tiles sells light landing. Slightly overblown where the floor pool and the lamp beam merge.

top_issues.issue: The Kindled does not read as 'made of light'
top_issues.why: Their bodies are darker than the core chamber's ambient orange, so the creature that should be the brightest thing in frame is one of the dimmest. At play size it reads as copper scaffolding.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make the body emissive white-gold, hotter than the chamber, with a stronger bloom and a cast pool that moves with it. Consider a whiter or paler hue so it separates from the core's orange.

top_issues.issue: Dark smudge / black halo behind the Kindled
top_issues.why: A soft black disc behind a light creature reads as a rendering artifact (an inverted glow or a depth-sorted sprite), not as design.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Remove it, or if it is an intended 'light-eating' aura, make it shaped and deliberate rather than a soft blob.

top_issues.issue: The Geode Mimic does not read as an ore
top_issues.why: It floats free of the rock as a violet crystal spider, so the 'ore that bites' fantasy (a tile you mistake for loot) is lost, and the dark-violet legs vanish into the dark.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Seat it against or half in a rock face, with its crystal crown matching a real ore glow so it reads as loot until it opens. Lift the leg value one step and let the cyan crown cast a coloured pool on the stone.

top_issues.why: Its light is a neutral grey halo that barely tints the stone, unlike the house-style warden or shellbacks, whose colour washes their surroundings.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give the halo the creature's cyan/violet hue and a real point light so adjacent faces pick it up.

top_issues.suggested_direction: Seat it in the rock face as an ore lookalike, hue its point light cyan/violet, and lift the leg value.
